title: Nuclear Magnetic Resonance Spectroscopy (Summary)
notes: Written by Kyle Crabtree; the chapter's learning objectives, which the book prints on this page, are kept here.

footnotes.html: The second “NMR” means proton NMR, <sup>1</sup>H NMR, which the three reasons that follow are about.

This chapter's pages do not teach the commutation relations of the spin operators, how a spectrometer's frequency follows from its field, perturbation theory for coupled protons, or the variational treatment of second-order spectra; the objectives and skill goals that name them refer to material the built pages leave out.
